title: `st.metric` docs promise gray for a zero delta but only the literal string `"0"` counts for strings, and the bundled skill's examples are all strings
body: ### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues. - [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue. - [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue. ### Summary This is a documentation inconsistency, not a runtime bug. The behavior is by design (#15790, closing #15005), and this report does not ask to change it. It asks for the two places that describe `delta` to match it. The `delta` docstring gives four unqualified rules ([metric.py lines 150-158](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/elements/metric.py#L150-L158)): no arrow for `None` or an empty string, "if the delta is zero, no arrow is shown and the delta is gray", red and down for "a negative number or starts with a minus sign", otherwise green and up. `delta_color="normal"` repeats "gray when zero" ([metric.py line 170](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/elements/metric.py#L170)) and `delta_arrow="auto"` says "no arrow is shown if `delta` is zero" ([metric.py line 269](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/elements/metric.py#L269)). Those rules treat strings as first-class input (the minus-sign branch exists only for strings), so a reader expects a zero-valued string such as `"0%"` or `"+0.0%"` to be "zero". The implementation defines zero for strings as the literal `"0"` only ([metric.py lines 598-604](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/elements/metric.py#L598-L604)), with the comment "other numeric-looking strings (e.g. `"0.0"`, `"0%"`) stay positive". #15790 added that deliberately, on the basis that string deltas are opaque display text, and locked it in with an anti-regression test. The docstring was not updated to say so, which is the gap. The packaged `developing-with-streamlit` skill widens the gap in practice. Every `st.metric` example in it passes `delta` as a pre-formatted string: [dashboards.md line 17](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/.agents/skills/developing-with-streamlit/references/dashboards.md?plain=1#L17), [dashboards.md lines 47-49](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/.agents/skills/developing-with-streamlit/references/dashboards.md?plain=1#L47-L49), and [data-display.md line 363](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/.agents/skills/developing-with-streamlit/references/data-display.md?plain=1#L363). The skill never mentions zero, so it does not contradict anything, but an agent that follows its examples and then reads the docstring's "gray when zero" will format a flat period as `"0%"` and get a green up-arrow. ### Reproducible Code Example ```Python For reference only. This shows the designed behavior, not a bug; it is here so the mismatch with the docstring wording can be seen without reading the source. import streamlit as st col1, col2, col3 = st.columns(3) # What the skill's examples lead to for a flat period: col1.metric("Orders (skill style)", "1.4k", "0%") # green up-arrow col2.metric("Orders (skill style)", "1.4k", "-0.0%") # red down-arrow # What actually renders neutral: col3.metric("Orders (numeric)", 1400, 0, delta_description="vs last month") "I.e.:" from streamlit.elements.metric import _is_zero_delta for delta in ["0", "0%", "+0.0%", "-0.0%", 0]: repr(delta), _is_zero_delta(delta) # '0' True # '0%' False # '+0.0%' False # '-0.0%' False # 0 True ``` ### Steps To Reproduce 1. Read the `delta` docstring's "if the delta is zero" rule and `delta_color="normal"`'s "gray when zero". 2. `streamlit run` or `uv run streamlit run` the snippet. 3. Compare the first two tiles with the third / see the debug output beneath it. ### Expected Behavior Documentation that states the actual rule: 1. In the `delta` docstring (and the `delta_color` / `delta_arrow` mentions of zero), say that a string delta is displayed as-is and that only the literal string `"0"` is treated as zero; other zero-like strings follow the sign rule (leading minus is negative, anything else is positive). One sentence is enough. 2. In the packaged skill, either show at least one example with a numeric `delta` and qualifier text in `delta_description=`, or add a one-line note next to the string examples that string deltas are never treated as zero. ### Current Behavior The docstring says zero deltas are gray with no qualification about strings. `"0%"` renders as a positive delta with a green up-arrow and `"-0.0%"` as a negative delta with a red down-arrow, which is the designed behavior. The skill's examples are all strings and say nothing about zero. For at-a-glance reference: ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version. Not a regression and not a behavior change request. Verified on 1.63.0 and 1.64.0 (the latest release at the time of writing): the docstring text, the skill examples, and `_is_zero_delta` are identical in both, and unchanged at the current tip of `develop`. ### Debug info - Streamlit version: 1.63.0 and 1.64.0, both reproduced - Python version: 3.14.6 - Operating System: Linux Mint 22.3 Zena 64-bit - Browser: Version 152.0.7977.82 (Official Build) for Linux Mint (x86_64) ### Additional Information The behavior was settled in #15790: the PR description lists an anti-regression test that `"0.0"`, `"+0"` and `"0%"` "stay green/up", and review confirmed the numbers-versus-strings split as intended. Nothing here asks to reopen that; it asks for the docstring and the skill to describe it. `format=` is not a way around the string question: it is one format applied to both `value` and `delta`, and `"percent"` multiplies by 100, so a tile whose value is a count and whose delta is a percent change cannot be served by a single `format=`. Numeric `delta` plus `delta_description=` is the pattern that works, and it is the one the skill could show.

comments.body:
**If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-17029)

This is a documentation mismatch, not a runtime defect. `_is_zero_delta` in `lib/streamlit/elements/metric.py` treats a numeric `0` (including `0.0` / `Decimal("0")`) and only the literal string `"0"` as zero; other zero-looking strings such as `"0%"`, `"0.0"`, and `"+0"` stay positive, and a leading minus (e.g. `"-0.0%"`) is negative. That split was intentional in #15790 (closing #15005) and is locked in by `test_zero_like_strings_keep_positive_direction`. The `delta` / `delta_color` / `delta_arrow` docstrings still say an unqualified “gray when zero,” and every `st.metric` example in the bundled `developing-with-streamlit` skill passes a pre-formatted string `delta`, so an agent that formats a flat period as `"0%"` gets a green up-arrow. The requested fix is to state the string rule in the docstring and show a numeric `delta` plus `delta_description=` (or a one-line note) in the skill.

### Related Issues

- [#15005](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/15005) (closed by [#15790](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/15790)): original request for gray/no-arrow zero deltas. That PR introduced the numbers-vs-strings split and the anti-regression tests; this issue is the leftover docstring/skill gap from that change, not a request to reopen the behavior.
- [#4775](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/4775) (closed): string deltas still get an up-arrow (e.g. `"No difference compared to last month"`). Same opaque-string rule; later addressed for control via `delta_arrow`, not by parsing zero-like strings.
- [#13690](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/13690) (closed): added `delta_description`, which is the pattern this report recommends for a numeric zero delta with qualifier text instead of stuffing `"0%"` into `delta`.
